::: {#def-dag .theorem}
## Directed acyclic graph

A graph $\mathcal{G}$ whose nodes represent the random variables $\mathbf{V}$ and whose directed edges, written $X\to Y$, form no cycles: no sequence of edges leads from a variable back to itself.

$X$ is a parent of $Y$ if $\mathcal{G}$ has an edge $X\to Y$; the set of parents of $Y$ is written $\mathbf{Pa}(Y)$. The ancestors of $Y$ are its parents, their parents, and so on.

A topological order of $\mathcal{G}$ is an ordering $V_1,\dots,V_m$ of $\mathbf{V}$ in which every parent precedes its children,

$$
\mathbf{Pa}(V_j)\subseteq\{V_1,\dots,V_{j-1}\}\quad\text{for every } j.
$$

Topological orders are not unique, and they need not be chronological.
:::
